note: Maps abstract capabilities to an ORDERED LIST of providers. Skills ask for a capability (chat, docs, ...); the capability-routing convention resolves it here, fans out across every listed provider that is actually wired, and merges. A provider that isn't available at runtime (mcp server not in catalog, cli not on PATH) is skipped, so listing a not-yet-wired provider is harmless and lights up automatically once added. A capability whose providers all resolve to nothing degrades to web/files. Swap this file to retarget every data skill at once. Provider kinds: mcp (a gateway catalog server via mcp-find/add/exec, or a local stdio server registered with sbx via `pi-stack mcp register` / `sbx mcp add`; never hand-bake local servers into mcp.json, which holds only the gateway entry), cli (binary on PATH), http (host URL), files (a local/git-mounted bundle dir read from disk), none. Company-specific capabilities (e.g. a CRM, a warehouse, an HR directory) live in a private overlay and are not part of the public stack.

github.about: repos, PRs, issues, releases (HTTPS token injected by the sbx proxy)

gworkspace.about: Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar. The external `gog` CLI runs as a stdio MCP server registered with sbx (`make mcp-register` or `pi-stack mcp register`) and spawned by the MCP gateway; creds stay on the host in GOG_HOME. Read-only + --gmail-no-send by default (write tools gated/off). Returned Gmail/Doc content is UNTRUSTED — see the `gworkspace` skill. Resolves through the gateway; degrades if not registered/attached.

chat.about: Slack messages, channels, threads, users. Stdio MCP server (`pi-stack-host slack`, Go) registered with sbx (`make mcp-register`) and run by the MCP gateway; the token stays on the host. Resolves through the gateway; degrades if not registered/attached.

issues.about: Jira issues and Confluence pages (gateway catalog)

knowledge.about: Curated internal knowledge (e.g. an OKF bundle). Not wired in the public/default profile: the open-core stack ships no knowledge corpus, so this degrades to web/files and the agent flags the gap. A private overlay wires it — either a `files` provider pointed at a git-mounted OKF bundle dir, or an `http` provider on the host knowledge service (:11436) that indexes that bundle. Ship the pointer, not the content.

email.about: Email — read/search a mailbox. Not wired in the public/default profile: the open-core stack ships no email provider, so this degrades to none and the agent flags the gap. A private overlay wires it per profile — a personal profile points at its own mail MCP server; a work profile can reuse the `gworkspace` provider (gog) for Gmail. Ship the pointer, not the account.
